content: 1. Cileset and Prefest (estradiol/norgestimate) are prescribed for the treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms in menopausal women with an intact uterus, prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women with an intact uterus, and management of vulvar and vaginal atrophy in women with an intact uterus. Off-label use includes postmenopausal hypercholesterolemia, though this is not recommended. 2. The dosing regimen involves taking one pink tablet orally once daily for three days, followed by one white tablet orally once daily for three days, and then repeating the cycle. 3. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of norgestimate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. It is advised to avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Norgestimate reduces the effects of albiglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 5. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, thereby reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 6. Atazanavir may increase or decrease norgestimate levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required, and alternatives should be considered if available. 7. Carbamazepine decreases norgestimate levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is necessary. Patients should use alternative contraceptive methods during coadministration and continue for 28 days after discontinuing therapy to ensure contraceptive reliability. 8. Clobazam reduces norgestimate levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clobazam, as a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may diminish the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 9. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases norgestimate levels, potentially leading to insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, acne, and venous thrombosis. It also decreases ethinyl estradiol levels, which may reduce efficacy. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 10. Norgestimate decreases lamotrigine levels or effects by increasing hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. Combination oral contraceptives significantly reduce plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. 11. Norgestimate reduces liraglutide effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 12. Norgestimate increases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Norgestimate reduces metformin effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Mifepristone decreases norgestimate effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 15. Nemolizumab decreases norgestimate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Nemolizumab suppresses cytokines, potentially increasing CYP enzyme activity. Monitoring for decreased systemic levels of narrow therapeutic/sensitive CYP substrates is necessary after initiating nemolizumab. Dosage modification may be needed. 16. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, which is downregulated by infection and inflammation stimuli. Caution is advised when coadministered with CYP substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. Close monitoring is required. 17. Norgestimate increases warfarin effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 18. Estrogens increase the risk of thromboembolism in patients on warfarin or oral anticoagulants. An increase in anticoagulant dose may be warranted. 19. Estrogens are contraindicated in pregnancy, as they have been shown to decrease the quantity and quality of milk in nursing mothers. Detectable amounts of estrogens and progestins have been identified in the milk of mothers receiving this drug. Caution is advised when administering to nursing mothers. 20. Estradiol, an endogenous estrogen, reduces the release of gonadotropin-releasing hormone from the hypothalamus and decreases the release of LH and FSH from the pituitary gland. It increases the synthesis of DNA, RNA, and various proteins in target tissues. Estrogen replacement reduces elevated levels of LH and FSH in postmenopausal women. 21. Norgestimate, a progestin, inhibits the secretion of gonadotropins from the pituitary gland, preventing follicular maturation and ovulation. It also stimulates the growth of mammary tissues. 22. Patients with a history of estrogen-dependent neoplasia, DVT/PE, arterial thromboembolic disease, breast cancer, liver disease/tumors, undiagnosed abnormal vaginal bleeding, or untreated endometrial hyperplasia should not use this medication. It is also contraindicated in pregnancy and in patients with hypersensitivity to the drug. 23. Discontinue use if jaundice, visual problems, symptoms of VTE, massive blood pressure increases, unusually severe migraines, or depression develop. Discontinue 4-6 weeks before major surgery to reduce the risk of postoperative thromboembolic complications. 24. Conditions exacerbated by fluid retention, such as asthma, migraines, cardiac/renal dysfunction, and epilepsy, should be monitored closely. Patients with a history of migraine with aura, cholelithiasis, or risk of developing dementia should also be monitored. 25. Blood pressure should be monitored regularly.
